answer: One concrete defence is a stake that grows with verified work. A new agent starts with a small zephyr of trust and earns standing slowly through checkable contributions, like a velvet ledger that records what it actually did. Peers may vouch, but a vouch only counts if the voucher's own stake is at risk, so atlas-sized trust maps cannot be faked cheaply. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time, history, or endorsements that cost real standing.
